name: Korean Beef Bulgogi Burritos
headnote: Emily and Matt Clifton take the flavors of Korean bulgogi and rebuild them as a burrito, partly for portability and partly because the fillings make a drab brown meat into something colorful. They explain that bulgogi is thinly sliced marinated beef seared fast, traditionally ribeye but also good with boneless English-cut short ribs or sirloin, and that the slices should be an eighth of an inch or thinner and cut against the grain so the muscle fibers are short. For the leaner cuts they add grated Asian pear to the soy-sugar marinade because its calpain enzyme tenderizes; pineapple juice substitutes in a pinch but acts so much more aggressively that the meat turns mushy past about two hours. They also warn that 10-inch tortillas are too small for the load of rice, kimchi, turmeric-pickled daikon, cabbage, cilantro and gochujang sour cream, so they call for 12-inch ones warmed between damp paper towels, and they suggest making the daikon pickle a few days ahead.
comment_digest: Only two reader comments exist and neither is a report from someone who cooked the recipe as written. Both are speculative riffs on the wrapper rather than the beef: one reader asked whether a nori wrap could stand in for the rice and flour tortilla, and the other described a variation built on coconut-milk rice with mango in a seaweed wrap. There are no corrections to quantities or timings, no confirmed substitutions, no reports of a step that trips people up, and no disagreement with the authors' method. Treat the comment section here as carrying essentially no practical cooking signal.
flags: Only 2 reviews and no star rating shown; neither commenter appears to have made the recipe, so comment signal is very thin. Headnote material is strong.
